items.title: SYNAPS-I demonstrates autonomous X-ray imaging and rapid reconstruction
participants: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / Advanced Light Source (lead)
items.what_changed: Demonstrations selected imaging targets autonomously, reconstructed ptychographic images at 200 per second, and produced a microchip reconstruction using roughly one tenth of the usual data.
items.significance: Could reduce beam time and radiation exposure while accelerating microelectronics and materials analysis.
items.affiliation_evidence: Brookhaven explicitly identifies SYNAPS-I as a ModCon seed project within DOE's Genesis Mission.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from the 33-item main archive and current science-discoveries review file; substantive experimental results.

items.title: Two Genesis projects target faster electric-grid planning
items.project: SI-assisted electromagnetic transient modeling and capacity-expansion scenario selection
items.what_changed: PNNL detailed two six-month projects: learning approximations for expensive grid-physics simulations and selecting informative scenarios from large capacity-expansion ensembles. These are research plans, not demonstrated speedups.
items.significance: Targets computational bottlenecks in grid reliability and expansion planning.
items.affiliation_evidence: PNNL explicitly states that both projects received Genesis Mission funding; its Genesis project page also lists this feature.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from archive and review file; different projects and substantive detail from the archived October 9 five-project feature.
